messages:
vik: quick allocator follow-up: I want to propose tenant-aligned slab leases + a 'soft-compact' signal instead of immediate global compaction. main goals: reduce full-compaction pauses, give tenants predictable eviction behavior, and let runtime prioritize critical threads.
alex: sounds promising. how are leases different from current soft-reserve tokens?
vik: leases are timebound ownership records for a slab region. API has AcquireLease(tenant, size, ttl) and ReleaseLease(lease). runtime can mark lease as 'soft-compactable' when fragmentation grows; compaction only happens after lease TTL or explicit Reclaim.
tara: TTL semantics worry me for long-running sessions (chat streams). we can't blindly reclaim mid-request.
vik: agreed. we add a Renew(lease) fastpath that is lock-free and tenant-local for hot allocations. renew keeps the slab pinned for the session.
jun: what about cross-tenant fairness? one noisy tenant could hog slabs by renewing aggressively.
vik: we pair leases with per-tenant credit budgets and a decay window. Renew consumes credits proportional to size; credits replenish slowly. noisy tenants hit reduced renew rate and thus are more likely to be demoted.
alex: metrics to watch: percent of Renew rejections, compaction duration, p95 latency spikes during compact. also need slab hotness heatmap.
tara: implementation detail: do we require per-slab metadata atomically updated on Acquire/Release? that could be expensive.
vik: idea: per-core compact counters + epoch tags. Acquire bumps a local counter and tags the slab epoch. A global sampler reconciles counters for compaction candidates. avoids global lock on every op.
jun: tradeoff: sampler adds eventual consistency; compaction decisions may be slightly stale. probably acceptable.
vik: pilot API sketch:```rust
struct Lease { id: u64, slab_id: u32, owner: TenantId, expires_at: u64 }
fn acquire_lease(tenant: TenantId, size: usize, ttl_ms: u64) -> Result<Lease, AcquireError>
fn renew_lease(id: u64) -> bool // try fastpath, returns false if blocked
fn release_lease(id: u64)
fn mark_soft_compact(slab_id: u32)
```

alex: can we add an EmergencyHold(tenant) that prevents compaction for N seconds for critical flows? used by on-path latency threads.
vik: yes, EmergencyHold is a scoped override but consumes a different credit pool with hard limits. abuse will be rate-limited.
tara: compact heuristics: prefer slabs with low active-renew ratio and high fragmentation score. we should avoid compaction of slabs backing small-kv caches.
jun: evict policy: when reclaiming from a slab, prefer demote -> move to host staging (async) before full free. that reduces immediate OOMs for other threads.
alex: staging has costs. who pays? we need a cost-estimate in the reclaim path so the scheduler can decide to demote vs free.
vik: agreed — estimate cost = bytes_demoted * demote_latency_per_byte + expected_reclaim_wait_ms. scheduler picks cheapest path to respect p99 SLO.
tara: rollout plan: 1) simulation mode in dev cluster (no effect, emit metrics) 2) enable soft-compact flags in test cluster with small tenants 3) canary on a handful of dedicated hosts 4) broad enable after 3 days of stable metrics. revert if compact duration > 200ms or p99 increases > 2%.
jun: telemetry: include sample traces with request-id, slab_id, lease_age, renew_count, tenant_id, and fragmentation_score. that helped before to root-cause noisy tenants.
alex: backward compatibility: expose tiny compatibility shim: AcquireLease translates to Reserve+Pin for older alloc API. deprecate older API after 1 quarter.
devops-bot: scheduled: lease-pilot branch -> perf-cluster @ 03:30 UTC. smoke tests queued.
devops-bot: smoke-tests: PASS. canary window opens now.
vik: thanks — I'll open the RFC appendix with the API, credit model, and compaction heuristic pseudocode. ping me for pairing on the sampler microbench. :slightly_smiling_face:
